current.text: The Clippers do not control their own first-round pick this season. It goes to the Thunder. They also lack future picks after losing five first-round picks in an NBA ruling.
Tanking does not help the Clippers, and the owner will not tank.
The team's motivation this season is unclear. The expected approach is to stay somewhat competitive to attract free agents while developing young players.
The team has little reason to win and little reason to lose, so it might rest Darius Garland.
The roster is one of the weakest in the league, and the team is expected to struggle. The low win total supports this.
This looks like a trial season, with long rotations and many players tested.
The roster has been reset. Harden, Zubac, Kawhi Leonard, Collins, Bogdanovic and Batum are gone. Ingram, Garland, Hachimura, Wagler and Max Strus are new.
Brandon Ingram, Bradley Beal, Jordan Miller and Yanic Konan Niederhauser are all out injured.
The Clippers are probably the most injury-hit team in the league.
The projected starting five is Darius Garland, Max Strus, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson. The expert is not confident about it.
The projected bench order is Kris Dunn sixth and Bradley Beal seventh, with Brook Lopez as backup center, Keaton Wagler as backup point guard and Kobe Sanders tenth.
The database depth chart (Lopez, Hachimura, Garland, Ingram, Wagler) does not match the newest expert projection. This is another sign that the rotation is not settled.
Isaiah Jackson is starting over Brook Lopez in preseason scrimmages.
Jackson keeping the starting center job is not guaranteed.
Zubac has been traded. The center options are 39-year-old Brook Lopez, Isaiah Jackson and the injured Yanic Konan Niederhauser.
The roster is not built to hand the offense to rookies. Garland and Ingram will do nearly everything.
The team will play several low-usage players, which leaves room for Ingram's usage to rise.
Rui Hachimura replacing John Collins is probably an offensive downgrade.
The projected lineup is weak on defense when Kris Dunn is not in it.
The fantasy playoff schedule is good: 4, 3 and 4 games in weeks 19 to 21, with only two back-to-back pairs.
The Clippers have 13 back-to-backs, the fewest in the league, so the risk of rest days for their players is lower.

durable.text: Coach Ty Lue makes unusual rotation choices and then changes them.
Lue's rotation changes make Clippers roles frustrating to predict for fantasy.

note: The Clippers are a weak, injury-hit team. They do not own their pick, so they have no reason to tank, and their playoff schedule (4-3-4 games, fewest back-to-backs in the league) is strong. Darius Garland gains the most because he and an injured Ingram will carry the offense, but the team might rest him since it has little to play for. Early on, watch the center battle between Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez and how Ty Lue shapes his long, changing rotation.
